title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Introduction (summary of Fig. 1); Fig. 1b-j; Supplementary Fig. 5b,c (intact flies)
quote: we found that the adult MDNs drive coordinated changes in stepping patterns across all three pairs of legs, with the strongest impact on the hindlegs.
mapping_basis: The paper's name MDN (Moonwalker Descending Neurons) is itself the MANC type name MDN (type_list.csv: MDN, DNp50).
stimulation: 5-s constant 660 nm red light (laser via fibre), ~0.73 mW/mm2
sensory_condition: tethered on air-supported 6-mm ball, side-view high-speed video (200 fps), DeepLabCut joint tracking
frequency_note: Supplementary Fig. 5c source data, intact flies: mean backward step frequency ~2.2 Hz hindleg, ~1.9 Hz midleg, ~3.5 Hz foreleg (N = 7)
coordination_notes: Joint flexion/extension phase coupling reversed relative to forward walking; hindlegs take longer, higher strides and provide main propulsion; after tarsal amputation, amputated legs continued to oscillate (hindleg oscillation frequency increased).
n_flies_note: N = 7 flies for Fig. 1b-h and Supp. Fig. 5c intact group; n = 6 flies per amputation group (Fig. 1i,j)
notes: MDN-1-GAL4 = VT044845-ZpGAL4DBD (attP40); VT050660-p65ADZp (attP2) (Supplementary Table 2, Fig. 1 and Supp. Fig. 5); Methods state it drives expression 'specifically in MDNs'. Flies first walked spontaneously, then backward walking was triggered by light. Fig. 1i,j tarsal-amputation experiments are on the same line and preparation and are folded into this record. effect_on_walking left not_assessed because flies were stimulated whether or not they were walking and the result is a direction switch (backward walking), not a speed/turn change.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, section 'LBL40 neurons trigger tibia flexion...'; Supplementary Fig. 5a,c (decapitated flies)
quote: optogenetic activation of the severed VNC projections of the MDNs induces backward walking, with its characteristically exaggerated hindleg movements
mapping_basis: The paper's name MDN is the MANC type name MDN (type_list.csv: MDN, DNp50).
frequency_note: Supplementary Fig. 5c source data, decapitated flies: mean backward step frequency ~1.25 Hz hindleg, ~1.2 Hz midleg, ~1.4 Hz foreleg; lower than intact for hind- and forelegs (p = 0.011, 0.0043)
coordination_notes: Supp. Fig. 5 title: 'The backward walking program is largely intact in decapitated flies.' Joint-angle traces show repeated steps in fore-, mid- and hindlegs during the 5-s stimulus.
n_flies_note: legend states N = 7 flies per group; source data list 8 decapitated values
notes: Same genotype as Fig. 1 (MDN-1-GAL4 = VT044845-ZpGAL4DBD; VT050660-p65ADZp; Supplementary Table 2 row 'Fig. 1 and Supplementary Fig. 5'). Decapitated tethered flies are normally stationary, so the stepping starts with stimulation.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Fig. 4b; Supplementary Fig. 3b (Fly Bowl, Empty-SS negative-control genotype)
quote: Robust backward walking was observed upon MDN activation in negative control flies, but completely abolished in both of the positive controls (Fig. 4b).
mapping_basis: The paper's name MDN is the MANC type name MDN (type_list.csv: MDN, DNp50).
stimulation: 627 nm red light, whole arena; nine 5-s episodes at 60-s intervals, 3 each at 0.158, 0.288 and 0.456 mW/mm2
sensory_condition: groups of ~25 flies in Fly Bowl, backlit infrared, 30 fps, Ctrax centroid tracking
other_cell_types: MANs (Moonwalker ascending neurons; the MDN split-LexA uses the MDN+MAN-1 enhancer combination)
n_flies_note: typically ~50 flies per genotype across two trials
notes: Negative-control genotype: MDN split-LexA > CsChrimson plus empty split-GAL4 (pBPp65ADZpUw; pBPZpGAL4DBDUw) > UAS-TNTe (Supplementary Table 2). Backward walking is measured as backward centroid distance (speed threshold >= 1.5 mm/s), without leg tracking, so confidence is medium. Methods: the split-LexA 'expressed in both MDNs and MANs but no other central neurons'. This is the activation arm of an epistasis screen; the 82 MF-line silencing genotypes are not records for MDN.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Methods, Behavioral assays; Fig. 7a-g (control trials and Empty-SS genotype); Supplementary Fig. 7c
quote: For SS > GtACR2 neuronal epistasis experiments, we first tested if a decapitated fly could walk backwards steadily during the 25-s red-light stimulus.
mapping_basis: The paper's name MDN is the MANC type name MDN (type_list.csv: MDN, DNp50).
stimulation: 25-s 660 nm red light, ~0.73 mW/mm2 (control trials: red only)
other_cell_types: MANs (Moonwalker ascending neurons; the MDN split-LexA uses the MDN+MAN-1 enhancer combination)
frequency_note: Fig. 7g source data, Empty-SS control trials: hindleg step frequency ~0.55-1.16 Hz per fly, mean ~0.77 Hz (N = 8)
coordination_notes: Only hindleg joint angles were tracked and quantified.
penetrance: flies were pre-selected for stable baseline backward walking throughout the 25-s stimulus
n_flies_note: Empty-SS N = 8; LBL40 and LUL130 genotypes N = 9 and 8 also received the same MDN activation in control trials
notes: The MDN-activation arm of an optogenetic epistasis experiment (CsChrimson in MDN, GtACR2 in LBL40/LUL130 or Empty-SS). Legs coded yes under the walking convention, but only hindlegs were tracked, and flies were pre-selected for steady backward walking, so confidence is medium. Supp. Fig. 7c: hindlegs amputated at the tarsus kept oscillating during MDN activation.

title: A dedicated brain circuit controls forward walking in Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Walking drive is flexibly suppressed or integrated'; Fig. 5c,d; Supplementary Fig. 5a,c
quote: Strikingly, MDN-activated flies always walked backward, rendering flies unable to cross the gap (Fig. 5c,d and Supplementary Fig. 5a).
mapping_basis: The paper's names MDN / DNp50 are the MANC type MDN and its listed literature synonym (type_list.csv).
stimulation: 1-s 625 nm red light, manually triggered (intensity not stated)
sensory_condition: gap-crossing assay, two 4-mm platforms 3.5 mm apart in a water-filled arena, wings clipped, side-view video at 150 Hz
penetrance: Supp. Fig. 5a: backward walking with probability ~1 in phases 0-3 (a small fraction fell in phase 2)
n_flies_note: Fig. 5c legend N = 4-13 MDN flies per phase; Supplementary Table 3: 13 female MDN flies
notes: Driver = VT044845-GAL4.DBD (attP40); VT050660-p65.AD (attP2) (Supplementary Table 2, 'MDN'), which is the MDN-1 hemidriver pair in driver_lines.csv. Specificity is not stated in this paper; Feng et al. 2020 (in this room) describe this line as MDN-specific. In phase 0 the flies stood in front of the gap before stimulation, so the stimulus started the backward walking. Supp. Fig. 5c: latency to move ~0.36 s. Supplementary Fig. 2b of this paper ranks DNs by connectome-predicted net excitation from RRN/BPN; this is the paper's own connectivity analysis, not an activation-simulation score, and I did not view that panel.
